coding_policy: Retain one primary observed failure-mode category for each failed trial so that category counts remain mutually exclusive; co-occurring or downstream problems may still exist. Where an existing assignment needs verification, retain its category and state the evidence limitation in the diagnosis or case notes without treating the assignment as newly confirmed.

Enumerate observable deviations, exclude deviations that the agent demonstrably recovered, and select the remaining mode with the clearest archived evidence link to the unsuccessful submission. If multiple candidates have such a link, chronology is only a deterministic tie-breaker; temporal precedence alone does not establish causality.
Use the issue description, candidate patch, reference patch, test patch, and trajectory together where available. A difference from the reference patch is not sufficient evidence of an error.
Artifact paths identify the materials available in this repository. They are navigation and provenance aids, not evidence that every listed artifact was necessary for every annotation.
Keep the archived outcome label separate from the qualitative diagnosis and do not infer a failure mode from the outcome alone.
Retain selected successful cases as a separate comparison set. Do not assign failure categories to them or include them in failure-category denominators.
Do not infer annotation agreement, independent assessment, semantic equivalence, or universal benchmark invalidity from the existence of a category assignment.
Do not invent supporting evidence or make a stronger claim than the retained issue, patches, trajectory, and evaluation requirements support.

values.SUPPORTED: The selected primary mode is the earliest observable unrecovered deviation, and archived patch, repository-state, tool, or evaluation evidence directly traces its retained effect to the unsuccessful submission.
values.NOT_SUPPORTED: The evidence identifies an earlier unrecovered deviation with an equally or more direct link to the unsuccessful submission than the selected mode, or contradicts the selected mode's proposed link.
values.INDETERMINATE: Missing evidence, multiple similarly supported explanations, or an unclear sequence prevents a defensible judgment.

attribution_audit.interpretation: This field audits support for the chronological attribution rule. It does not identify or prove a causal root cause.

categories.name: Misinterpretation / Domain Knowledge Lack
categories.definition: The annotated repair direction reflects an incomplete or incorrect interpretation of the issue's semantics, domain rules, or architectural assumptions.
categories.decision_rule: Use when the evidence identifies a mistaken requirement or domain interpretation as the primary breakdown. Cite the specific overlooked constraint; do not infer a general absence of domain knowledge from a failed patch alone.

categories.name: Distracted by Hints / TODOs
categories.definition: The annotated repair follows a suggestion or nearby TODO that does not address the issue's required behavior.
categories.decision_rule: Use when the evidence links the chosen repair direction to an identifiable hint, suggestion, or TODO and explains the remaining defect. Describe observed reliance on that cue without claiming a counterfactual causal effect or a model-wide tendency.

categories.name: Incomplete Scope / Wrong Layer
categories.definition: The repair targets only part of the required implementation scope or attempts the change at an architectural layer that cannot provide the complete behavior.
categories.decision_rule: Use when the primary failure concerns omitted files, entry points, subclasses, or an unsuitable intervention layer. Distinguish this from S1, which concerns incomplete behavior or logic after the relevant location has been identified.

categories.name: Partial Fix / Incomplete Logic
categories.definition: The selected repair logic covers some required scenarios but leaves a relevant operation, parameter combination, boundary case, or compatibility condition unresolved.
categories.decision_rule: Use when the failure centers on incomplete behavioral coverage rather than primarily missing a code location. Identify the covered and uncovered scenarios without treating all patch omissions as localization failures.

categories.name: Incorrect Repair Strategy
categories.definition: The selected algorithm or transformation fails to implement the target operation's required behavior or project constraint.
categories.decision_rule: Assign S2 when the selected repair strategy leaves the target operation incorrect. Assign V3 instead when the reported local defect is addressed and tests or repository evidence confirm that this repair breaks another previously valid input, caller contract, or state lifecycle; describe the overly broad strategy as a secondary observation. Breadth, a reference-patch difference, a failed outcome, or test membership in FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS alone is insufficient. A local fix can coexist with other target defects.

categories.name: Hardcoding / Bad Practices
categories.definition: The repair uses a fixed or environment-specific implementation that fails to satisfy the required portability or repository convention.
categories.decision_rule: Use when the saved diagnosis identifies a concrete hardcoded assumption or replacement for a required abstraction and links it to unsupported behavior. Style differences or a preference for a library implementation alone do not establish failure.

categories.name: Tool Failure / Silent State Hallucination
categories.definition: An editing or execution operation fails, produces an unintended change, or leaves the agent acting on an incorrect belief about the actual repository state.
categories.decision_rule: Require concrete tool or state evidence, such as a failed command, an unexecuted edit, a mismatch between an intended edit and the resulting file, or an unsupported claim that a change was applied. Unrelated patch content or benchmark failure alone is insufficient.

categories.name: Specification-Oracle Gap
categories.definition: The annotation identifies a difference between the behavior emphasized by the issue description and the additional requirements enforced by the benchmark tests.
categories.decision_rule: State the requirement expressed in the issue and the additional tested condition. Do not declare the patch semantically correct or the test invalid solely because the requirement is implicit. Use V2 when the primary distinction is an exact representation or formatting assertion.

categories.name: Strict Output Format Mismatch
categories.definition: The recorded evaluation distinguishes the patch's output or representation from the expected string, argument structure, serialized form, or attribute representation.
categories.decision_rule: Identify the concrete expected and produced representations. Keep representation mismatch separate from a broader missing behavioral requirement in V1. Do not presume semantic equivalence: formatting can be an externally observable contract and requires case-specific analysis.

categories.name: Regression of Existing Behavior
categories.definition: The patch addresses the reported local defect but demonstrably breaks another previously valid input, caller contract, or state lifecycle.
categories.decision_rule: Identify the prior valid behavior and the patch-induced change using tests or repository evidence. Prefer V3 over S2 when an overly broad repair strategy produces that confirmed regression, even if secondary target defects coexist. This preference does not apply to unrelated or recovered errors and does not establish causality. A local reproduction alone does not prove complete correctness; patch breadth, a reference-patch difference, or a failed outcome alone does not prove regression. Existing assignments awaiting verification remain in their categories with the evidence limitation stated in the diagnosis or case notes.

categories.name: Execution Timing Mismatch
categories.definition: The annotation concerns a repair applied at a lifecycle point or processing stage that differs from when the surrounding framework or evaluation expects the required behavior.
categories.decision_rule: Identify when the required state or transformation is expected and when the patch actually supplies it. Use this category only when the saved evidence establishes a timing or processing-stage distinction.
